sg.ra: Choose Center Orchestra rows B-H for close, head-on views without side angles or the mezzanine overhang.
Choose Rows A or B for some of the theater’s best views and a panoramic look at the stage. Expect premium pricing in these front rows. Row A also has a little extra legroom.
The side Orchestra offers a decent view for a reasonable price.

sn.c: In the Center Orchestra, the Front Mezzanine overhangs from row H, so seats behind it can lose action at the top of the stage.
sn.sh: Overhang from row H trims the top of the stage

sn.c: The sides of the Orchestra give a decent view for a reasonable price, though more of the stage is blocked toward the outer edge.
sn.sh: Decent view for a fair price on the sides

sn.c: The middle and back of the Center Front Mezzanine are good value, with a decent rake between rows.
sn.sh: Raked middle and back rows for less

sn.lo: Center Rear Mezzanine, rows A to B
sn.c: Rows A and B toward the center of the Rear Mezzanine are very good value, with direct views down to the stage.
sn.sh: Direct views at a good price

sn.c: Row K in the Left and Right Orchestra has an aisle in front of it, giving extra legroom.
The Rear Mezzanine is the farthest level from the stage, so fine details are harder to make out.

vs.sum: The Majestic Theatre is one of Broadway's most storied houses, but its 1,645-seat scale means rear and side sections have meaningful sightline limitations and obstructed views. Legroom is tight and restrooms insufficient for the volume, though the historic ambiance is genuine.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair locations in Orchestra. No steps to rows AA-H. Infrared devices available.
